claims.text: Machine-learning potentials can be trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Such machine-learning potentials can improve the representation of atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid alloy states.
The proposed method applies at temperatures near and above the alloys' melting points.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing multiple principal elements.
Improved representation of atomic configurations leads to better reference–target phase-space overlap.
Better reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be lower with the machine-learning reference than with TOR-TILD's EAM references.
TOR-TILD uses EAM reference potentials as the relevant baseline.
Agreement of solid–liquid free-energy differences with ab initio calculations can be compared between machine-learning potentials and TOR-TILD EAM references.
Failure of the machine-learning potential to improve agreement with ab initio free-energy differences relative to the EAM reference would falsify the hypothesis.
